column1: # Kan-Eng glyph table: Kan-EngPraja, Kan-EngDeepa, Kan-EngKarn, Kan-EngVani and
# Kan-EngUsha, which share 1 layout. The fonts are bilingual: Latin letters and digits
# at the ASCII codes, Kannada at the ASCII symbol codes $ & % < ] ^ ` { } ~ and from 81
# The format is described in src/legacy/table.rs. Codes are Windows-1252 bytes; 81, 8D,
# 8F, 90 and 9D, which Windows-1252 leaves undefined, stand for themselves.
# Derived from documents, as no code page is published. The glyphs were rendered from
# the Kan-Eng TrueType fonts embedded in 45 Karnataka budget papers of 2002 to 2014 on
# kar.nic.in/finance, made with Acrobat PDFMaker for Excel and Acrobat Distiller and
# fetched from the Internet Archive. Acrobat put the glyphs at codes Windows-1252
# leaves undefined, and at AD, in a second, CID-keyed copy of each font, whose
# ToUnicode map gives the code (U+009D for 9D, U+2212 for AD). The copy's glyph IDs
# are the code minus 30 (decimal), as in every subset's own cmap from 7E to C0.
# Those codes were read from the words they appear in: 81 ಆ (ಆಯವ್ಯಯ), 9D ಚ
# (ವೆಚ್ಚ), 90 subscript ಮ (ಚೆನ್ನಮ್ಮ), AD subscript ಣ (ಸಣ್ಣ, ಉಣ್ಣೆ, ಕೃಷ್ಣ); 8D ಃ by
# its shape, as its 1 use is a typing error. Each glyph was identified by eye, then checked in context: the papers'
# Kannada text, 833 distinct lines in drawing order, was converted, and every unknown
# glyph and malformed syllable was read against the codes rendered with the embedded
# docs/kan-eng.md has the method and results.
# Codes no document used are left out, and are reported as unknown.
